What Widely available does not promise

Baseline tells you

  • Works in every core browser
  • For 30 months or more

Still check

  • Most sites, not all
  • Older browsers your users run

Use the label to plan, then check your own users.

Can you use a web feature today?

Baseline answers with one label.

Baseline checks seven core browsers: Chrome on desktop and Android, Edge,

Firefox on desktop and Android, and Safari on macOS and iOS.

A feature starts as Limited availability.

When the last core browser ships it, the feature is Newly available.

Thirty months later, it is Widely available.

The thirty month clock starts only when the last core browser ships.

Before that day, the feature stays Limited, however old it is.

The has selector became Newly available in December 2023.

Add thirty months, and it is Widely available in June 2026.

Can I use shows support for each browser.

Green means supported, red means not supported,

greenish yellow means partial, and gray means unknown.

Widely available means the feature works for most sites, not all.

If your users run older browsers, check their support yourself.
